summary: Sculk sensors are not activated upon placing food onto campfires
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft 1.18.2.
2. Create or enter a world.
3. Place a campfire.
4. Place a sculk sensor nearby.
5. Place food onto the campfire.
6. Observe whether the sculk sensor activates.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 20w51a, 21w03a, 21w05a, 21w05b, 21w06a, 21w07a, 21w08b, 21w10a, 21w14a, 21w15a, 21w17a, 21w19a, 21w20a, 1.17 Pre-release 1, 1.17 Pre-release 3, 1.17 Pre-release 5, 1.17 Release Candidate 1, 1.17 Release Candidate 2, 1.17, 1.17.1 Pre-release 1, 1.17.1 Pre-release 3, 1.17.1, 21w38a, 21w41a, 21w43a, 1.18, 1.18.1, 22w05a, 1.18.2, 22w14a, 22w17a, 22w18a, 1.19 Pre-release 1 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior:
When a player successfully places a valid cookable food item onto a campfire, the food is added to the campfire and its contents visibly change. However, this interaction does not emit a game event/vibration at the campfire’s position.

Consequently, a nearby sculk sensor does not detect the food-placement interaction and remains inactive, provided no other vibration is generated. This occurs even when the sensor is within its normal detection range and has a clear path to the campfire.
Expected Behavior: When food is placed onto a campfire, any nearby sculk sensor should detect the interaction as a vibration and activate accordingly. The sensor should respond consistently with other detectable actions, allowing it to produce its normal redstone signal when the campfire’s contents change.
